$comment: Roster of every surface OUTSIDE `infra/` that names the stale cluster tree.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (081M00QCHWA087G0R000GKKRXD):
The repo carries two declarations of one cluster. `full-ai-cluster/` is the
live one — it is what `zeta-install.sh` runs (`nixos-install --flake
/mnt/etc/zeta/full-ai-cluster#$HOST`) and the only flake CI evaluates.
`infra/k8s` + `infra/nixos` are the older declaration. They COLLIDE: both
declare Application/argocd/zeta-root with different spec.source.path and both
carry prune+selfHeal, so whichever is applied last prunes the other tree's
entire child graph. That collision is caught by single-node-readiness.ts and
is currently suppressed by an `acknowledgedRootAppDuplicates` entry.
The consolidation has now been deferred twice, both times for the same
reason: nobody could show that the list of things still reading the stale
tree was COMPLETE. A 2026-08-16 pass named two code consumers and called the
list closed; there were nine. This file makes that list a derived, checked
fact instead of a grep somebody ran once.
HOW IT IS CHECKED: audit-cluster-tree-consumers.ts derives the real set with
`git grep` and compares it to `consumers` below. A NEW reference to the stale
tree fails the audit (re-divergence). A rostered path that no longer
references it also fails (the roster must shrink as the migration lands, so
it can never over-claim). Deletion of `infra/k8s` + `infra/nixos` is provably
safe when every `blocking` and `derived` entry is gone.
THE DELETION ITSELF IS GATED on maintainer sign-off — see the work item's
`Done when` list. This roster does not authorize it; it makes it checkable.
$comment_excludedPrefixes: Prose archives and the stale tree itself. These are frozen records (merged
PR reviews, research ferries, work-item bodies) — rewriting them would
falsify history, and none of them is read by a machine. Named explicitly
rather than as a wildcard so the exclusion is auditable.
$comment_dispositions: blocking — deleting the stale tree BREAKS this, or makes it emit output that
points at a path that no longer exists. Must be migrated first.
derived  — mechanically follows the deletion (a roots list, an acknowledgement
entry). Edit in the same commit; nothing breaks if it lags.
prose    — a comment or document. Breaks nothing; correct for accuracy.
self     — this guard, its roster, and its mutation suite. They name the stale
tree because their subject IS the stale tree.

consumers.note: States the byte-lock toolchain (wabt, binaryen, emscripten, nodejs) is declared in infra/nixos/modules/common.nix. TRUE TODAY and it is the ONLY NixOS module that declares it — VERIFIED 2026-08-17: full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/common.nix contains none of wabt/binaryen/emscripten/zig/rustup. This is content unique to the stale tree, not a stale citation. MEASURED 2026-09-06, so the decision below needs no further digging: (a) the README enumerates FOUR declaration sites — NixOS, brew, apt, and the root flake devShell — and deleting infra/nixos removes only the NixOS one; (b) `full-ai-cluster/` declares the byte-lock toolchain NOWHERE (grep for wabt/binaryen/emscripten across the tree returns nothing), so the packages would simply be absent from cluster hosts; (c) bytelock.yml never runs on a cluster host — its matrix is ubuntu-24.04 / macos / windows GitHub runners and it installs wabt via apt, brew and choco. So no byte-lock work depends on the NixOS declaration today.
consumers.migrateTo: MAINTAINER DECISION, now cheap: either carry the byte-lock toolchain block into full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/common.nix (cluster hosts gain 4 packages they are not measured to need), or record on the record that cluster hosts do not need it and the root devShell + the three OS manifests are the declaration set. The evidence for the second is in the note above; this roster does not choose.
